recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Future genomics naming or modeling work should be handled through the active MolecularDefinition/Molecular Data Types issue trail, not by reopening this DSTU2 Sequence wording correction.
issue_request: FHIR-11306 was a Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics change request against the DSTU2 Sequence resource. The submitted text suggested renaming the resource toward genetic variation because the introduction implied a Sequence had at most one variation, but the accepted resolution narrowed the action to changing the website description because the single-variant wording was a typo.
initial_application: Git history did not show a Jira-tagged FHIR-11306 application commit; the only direct log hit was an unrelated SVN revision number. The requested wording appears to have been applied with neighboring issue FHIR-11307 in commit 54e60c59aa7079e0f7bf544e617b09edc183060c, which changed source/sequence/sequence-introduction.xml from 'at most one variation' and 'a sequence variation' to 'multiple variations' and 'sequence variations'.
additional_context: Sequence was later renamed to MolecularSequence for FHIR-19453, then the current checkout removed source/sequence and source/molecularsequence. Current source/fhir.ini lists Sequence under [removed-resources], does not list Sequence or MolecularSequence as active [resources], and only retains MolecularSequence in inactive/commented metadata. Current diagnostics text points readers from MolecularSequence to MolecularDefinition, whose inspected prose describes molecular entities and genetic variation use cases without the old single-variation restriction.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The final issue resolution was already satisfied in historical source, the affected resource is outside current build scope, and current source searches found no remaining old single-variant wording to correct.
